headline: Cognition in Talks for $75 Billion Value With New Funding
author: Rebecca Torrence

paragraphs.text: Fri, November 20, 2026 at 1:47 PM MST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- Artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. is in funding talks at a $75 billion valuation, just two months after announcing its most recent funding round, according to people familiar with the matter.
The company is considering raising $2 billion or more in the financing, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing private information.

The efforts are ongoing and details could change, the people said. If completed, the financing would be Cognition's third this year. It's already raised over $3 billion in 2026 so far, including over $2 billion at a $48 billion value in September.
Cognition didn't respond to requests for comment. Business Insider reported in October that Cognition was weighing a new fundraising effort.

The startup has surged this year as investors have piled into companies building AI agents for software development. Cognition and its flagship product, AI engineering agent Devin, compete with the likes of Cursor, which SpaceX acquired earlier this year for $60 billion. Several major Cursor backers, including Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, invested in Cognition after that acquisition closed.

Cognition, which sells to companies including Citigroup Inc. and Nvidia Corp., said in September that it was on track to reach $1 billion in annualized revenue, roughly doubling its run rate from four months prior.
